children: Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) cattle futures turned lower on Wednesday — with deferred feeder cattle futures falling sharply — after the U.S. government said it would reopen a key port to livestock trade next week that ​was closed because of New World ​screwworm.

U.S. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins ​said on Wednesday that the Department of ‌Agriculture is preparing to reopen the Santa Teresa, New Mexico, port of entry at the U.S.-Mexico border. The agency said that operations will start slowly with an initial limit of 750 head of cattle per day.

The USDA in late August resumed cross-border livestock ​trade with Mexico under a phased port reopening that ‌began ⁠in Douglas, Arizona, after months of closures due to concerns about the spread of the screwworm parasite.

Cattle futures are also coming under pressure later this week as traders adjust their positions ahead of Friday's monthly USDA Cattle on Feed report. Analysts surveyed by Reuters expected the government to report the number of cattle in U.S. feedlots as of September 1 at 11.268 million head, up 1.7% from a year ago.

"The question right now in the markets is not only about supply, but uncertainty over consumer demand," said Dan Norcini, an independent livestock trader. "With everything going on with gas and consumer goods prices, can we continue to push out high-priced beef? Because a lot of consumers are getting hit pretty hard by these fuel prices."

Meanwhile, nearly all lean hog futures contracts set fresh lows again on Wednesday, continuing a multi-day slump amid continued pressure from ample U.S. hog supplies and slumping consumer demand. But contracts ended the session mixed on technical trading, traders said.
"Pork demand is losing out to chicken at the grocery stores," Norcini said. "Like beef, the market is focused on consumers and consumer demand."

CME October lean hog futures (LHV26) settled down 0.0400 cent at 78.675 cents per pound after notching a contract low at 78.525 cents, and December hogs (LHZ26) ended up 0.300 cent at 69.950 cents after posting a contract low at 69.100 cents.
